# University of Jordan
The University of Jordan, established by royal decree in 1962, is the first and largest university in Jordan, with its main campus located in the Jubaiha area of Amman and a branch in Aqaba founded in 2009. The university has played a central role in national education, beginning with a single Faculty of Arts and growing rapidly to include scientific, medical, and humanities faculties. Today, it offers 78 undergraduate and 143 postgraduate programs across a wide range of disciplines. Notable historical developments include the early adoption of the credit hour system (reportedly the first in the Arab world), founding of several research centers, establishment of the Jordan University Hospital in 1973, and ongoing expansion of facilities and research activity. Its library dates from 1962 and houses over a million items, serving as an important national repository.
The university is highly ranked regionally, consistently appearing as Jordan's top institution in ratings such as Webometrics, QS, Times Higher Education, and ARWU. It is affiliated with many international organizations and maintains partnerships for student and faculty exchanges. Research output is supported by multiple centers and its own press, publishing peer-reviewed journals. The University of Jordan boasts numerous distinguished faculty and alumni, including leaders in politics, diplomacy, science, education, and culture—such as multiple Jordanian prime ministers, internationally renowned researchers, and prominent figures in public service, journalism, and the arts. Student life features a vibrant union, notable student activism, and a diverse range of academic and extracurricular activities.
